description: `platformAutomerge` hands the merge to GitHub's own auto-merge, which fires the moment the last REQUIRED check of the branch ruleset reports green — seconds, against the ≈hourly wait for Renovate to come back and merge the PR itself. It is safe here because the required set includes `gradle`, which builds: native auto-merge waits only on required checks, so a ruleset that required nothing meaningful would merge without waiting for CI at all. The shared preset leaves this false for exactly that reason; turning it on is a per-repository statement that the ruleset is real. Majors are still excluded by the first rule below, so this only accelerates the minor/patch/digest/pin updates.

packageRules.description: Majors are never automerged. `automerge: true` above is a blanket setting — the shared preset turns automerge on for minor/patch/digest/pin only, but a top-level `true` here covers every update type, so a major would land on green CI after its 14-day soak with nobody reading the diff. Keep the soak, drop the automerge; this is the posture m3-catalog and wear-m3-catalog already carry.

Compose Multiplatform lands as its own PR and is never automerged: a renderer bump moves the pixels under every preview this server renders, and `visual-harness` is the review — a human reads its result. This replaces a hold at the 1.11.x line that was already dead. #731 moved the catalog to 1.12.0 deliberately (no published module here declares a Compose dependency, so the bump raises no consumer floor), which left `matchCurrentValue: /^1\.11\./` matching nothing — a rule that reads as a pin while allowing 1.13 straight through on automerge. The patterns are the regex form rather than `org.jetbrains.compose{/,}**`, which is the npm-scope idiom and is not how a Maven `group:artifact` coordinate is matched. The floor this deliberately does NOT encode: compose-ai-tools and compose-preview-daemon are held at 1.11.x because their published bytecode targets it, so this repository sits one Compose line above the daemon it drives — read compose-preview-daemon's docs/RENDERER_COMPATIBILITY.md before taking 1.13.

ClassGraph 6 requires Java 25 and a new scanning API. PR #1741 fails checkServerJvmFloor (Java 17) and compilation at overrideClasspath. Keep updates below 6 while the server distribution supports Java 17; ClassGraph 5 remains eligible for a reviewed API migration. Remove this ceiling only after intentionally raising the server JVM floor to Java 25 and porting/verifying preview discovery. See https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/pull/1741 and https://github.com/classgraph/classgraph#classgraph-6-is-released.

Keep the Java 17 compatibility/build lane on 17 while allowing maintenance releases. The distribution's declared runtime floor and checkServerJvmFloor remain 17; replacing this lane with a newer JVM would remove coverage of that contract. Change only with an intentional floor migration and packaged startup verification. See docs/development/JAVA_VERSION_POLICY.md.

Keep the UI-builder render/visual-harness Java lane on 21, including maintenance releases. PR #1738 passed CI on 25 but did not migrate the Java 17 distribution floor or the Temurin 21 image. Adopt a new runtime in a separate reviewed migration with render/distribution evidence; an LTS label alone is not that decision. See docs/development/JAVA_VERSION_POLICY.md.

The shipped host image uses Java 21 for the UI-builder render bundle. Keep Temurin 21 maintenance tags and digest refreshes; moving to 25 requires the same deliberate runtime/render validation as the visual-harness lane. This does not change the distribution's Java 17 minimum. See docs/development/JAVA_VERSION_POLICY.md.
